name: Stujack Pass + Summit Scramble
approach: From I-5 exit 208, drive east on SR-530 through Arlington and continue about 28 miles to Darrington. At the four-way stop in town, turn right (south) onto the Mountain Loop Highway and follow it roughly 14 miles — paved, then graveled — to FR-2095 (the Mt. Pugh Spur Road), signed with a large prominent marker on the left. Turn left onto FR-2095 and continue about 1 mile to the Mt. Pugh Trailhead (#644) on the right; parking at the trailhead itself is very limited (a handful of cars), so the large pullout at the switchback just below the trailhead is a reliable overflow option. From the trailhead, Trail #644 climbs through deep old-growth forest with several stream crossings, gaining about 1,300 ft over 1.5 miles to Lake Metan, a small subalpine tarn that serves as the natural 'base' before the ascent steepens toward Stujack Pass.

waypoints.name: Mt. Pugh Trailhead #644
waypoints.note: Mountain Loop Highway to FR-2095. Trail passes Lake Metan (1.5 mi) en route to Stujack Pass.
waypoints.directions: From I-5 exit 208, drive east on SR-530 through Arlington to Darrington, about 28 miles, then turn right at the four-way stop in town onto the Mountain Loop Highway and follow it south roughly 14 miles — paved at first, then graveled — to FR-2095, the Mt. Pugh Spur Road, marked with a large sign on the left. Turn onto FR-2095, a narrow, one-lane, unpaved road, and continue about a mile to the trailhead on the right; the trailhead lot itself holds only a handful of cars, so use the large pullout at the switchback just below it if it's full. FR-2095 is gated from October 16 to June 1 for wildlife, on top of whatever winter closure may be in effect on the Mountain Loop Highway itself.

waypoints.name: Lake Metan
waypoints.directions: Follow Trail #644 about 1.5 miles through old-growth forest, with several stream crossings and about 1,300 ft of gain, to Lake Metan. It is the last reliable water on the route.

waypoints.name: Stujack Pass
waypoints.directions: Round the north side of the lake and switchback steeply up through forest, then talus and meadows past an open boulder basin near 4,900 ft, to the notch of Stujack Pass at about 5,700 ft, where the maintained trail ends. Snow often lingers on this stretch into midsummer.

waypoints.name: Mount Pugh Summit
waypoints.directions: Climb left out of the notch on heather, contour the east side of the ridge and cross the head of a small permanent snowfield, then follow the knife-edge crest on chipped, blasted ledges past the short Class 3 chimney with an iron ring. Ignore stray cairns that lead toward the cliff edge. The true high point is a roughly 10 ft boulder at the edge of the flat summit plateau.
